title: Proximal Map
comment: Proximal Map — The proximal map projects on a level set. For l^p norms, it is a thresholding operator shrinking toward 0. It induces sparsity for p smaller than 1. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proximal_operator
alt_text: Proximal Map. The proximal map projects on a level set. For l^p norms, it is a thresholding operator shrinking toward 0. It induces sparsity for p smaller than 1.

title: Simplicial Cpx
comment: Simplicial Cpx — Simplicial complexes are combinatorial objects generalizing triangulations. They are central to (computational) homology and topological data analysis. Two examples for embedded points are alpha and Chech complexes. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simplicial_complex
alt_text: Simplicial Cpx. Simplicial complexes are combinatorial objects generalizing triangulations. They are central to (computational) homology and topological data analysis. Two examples for embedded points are alpha and Chech complexes.

title: Inverse Kin
comment: Inverse Kin — Numerical inverse kinematics solves an ill-posed inverse problem (non-unique solution) by gradient descent, thereby leveraging an "implicit bias" (favoring minimal displacements). It is at the heart of robotics and CG animation. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inverse_kinematics
alt_text: Inverse Kin. Numerical inverse kinematics solves an ill-posed inverse problem (non-unique solution) by gradient descent, thereby leveraging an "implicit bias" (favoring minimal displacements). It is at the heart of robotics and CG animation.

title: Aniso Diffusion
comment: Aniso Diffusion — Anisotropic diffusion uses space-varyingg conductivity to slow down diffusion near edges, resulting in non-isotropic diffusion behavior. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anisotropic_diffusion
alt_text: Aniso Diffusion. Anisotropic diffusion uses space-varyingg conductivity to slow down diffusion near edges, resulting in non-isotropic diffusion behavior.

title: Toland Duality
comment: Toland Duality — Toland's duality for non-convex optimization (difference of convex functions) is surprisingly useful when the dual happens to be convex. A nice paper by Guillaume Carlier explores this concept. https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~carlier/toland.pdf
alt_text: Toland Duality. Toland's duality for non-convex optimization (difference of convex functions) is surprisingly useful when the dual happens to be convex. A nice paper by Guillaume Carlier explores this concept.

title: Kaczmarz Algo
comment: Kaczmarz Algo — Kaczmarz's algorithm corresponds to the iterative projection on the hyper-space defined by the columns. Here, the worst possible ordering of the constraints is displayed. Using random selection helps a lot. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaczmarz_method

title: Backprop
comment: Backprop — Back-propagation for feed-forward architecture is a special case of reverse-mode automatic differentiation. It computes the gradient of a loss function with a cost comparable to the computation of the loss function itself. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backpropagation
alt_text: Backprop. Back-propagation for feed-forward architecture is a special case of reverse-mode automatic differentiation. It computes the gradient of a loss function with a cost comparable to the computation of the loss function itself.

title: Nash
comment: Nash — Classic reference: J. Nash, The Imbedding Problem for Riemannian Manifolds, 1956, C^1 n-dimensional manifolds can be isometrically embedded in dimension 2n, defining "fractal" like surfaces. This contrasts with smooth manifolds (which requires n(n+2)/2 dimensions).

title: Boosting
comment: Boosting — Boosting methods compute a strong classifier as a weighted sum of weak classifiers. The optimization is performed by a greedy coordinate minimization. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boosting_(machine_learning

title: Jl Lemma
comment: Jl Lemma — The Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma shows that one can project linearly m points in dimension log(m)/epsilon^2 with distortion epsilon. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnson%E2%80%93Lindenstrauss_lemma
alt_text: Jl Lemma. The Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma shows that one can project linearly m points in dimension log(m)/epsilon^2 with distortion epsilon.

title: Kernel Svm
comment: Kernel Svm — Support vector machines (SVM) can be used to define curved decision boundaries using the kernel trick. It implicitly makes use of an infinite dimensional feature lifting. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kernel_method
alt_text: Kernel Svm. Support vector machines (SVM) can be used to define curved decision boundaries using the kernel trick. It implicitly makes use of an infinite dimensional feature lifting.

title: Delaunay
comment: Delaunay — Classic reference: B. Delaunay, Sur la sphere vide, 1934. Introduces the concept of Delaunay triangulation, which is the dual of the Voronoi diagram. The most fundamental tool of computational geometry. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delaunay_triangulation
alt_text: Delaunay. Classic reference: B. Delaunay, Sur la sphere vide, 1934. Introduces the concept of Delaunay triangulation, which is the dual of the Voronoi diagram. The most fundamental tool of computational geometry.

title: Voronoi Pruning
comment: Voronoi Pruning — Pruning the Voronoi diagram of a set of points is way to estimate the medial axis of a smooth curve. Used in many shape reconstruction methods. http://web.cs.ucdavis.edu/~amenta/pubs/crust.pdf
alt_text: Voronoi Pruning. Pruning the Voronoi diagram of a set of points is way to estimate the medial axis of a smooth curve. Used in many shape reconstruction methods.

title: Runge
comment: Runge — Classic reference: Carl Runge, Über empirische Funktionen und die Interpolation zwischen äquidistanten Ordinaten, 1901. Oscillations are introduced by polynomial interpolation at equi-spaced grid points. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runge%27s_phenomenon

title: Aliasing
comment: Aliasing — Classic reference: Franklin Crow, The aliasing problem in computer-generated shaded images, 1977. title: Floyd Warshall
comment: Floyd Warshall — Floyd-Warshall algorithm computes all pairs shortest distances. Related to iterative powering of the adjacency matrix for the (min, +) algebra from Tropical geometry. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Floyd%E2%80%93Warshall_algorithm
